correctness.rationale: For a fixed nonzero rectangle U×V the two products with an arbitrary X are U×W and Z×V, with W the column support of rows V of X and Z the row support of columns U of X. The equality is either W=Z=∅ or W=V and Z=U. The first case leaves exactly X[Vᶜ,Uᶜ] unconstrained. In the second, entries in V×Vᶜ and Uᶜ×U are forbidden; rows U must hit columns U and columns V must be hit by rows V. Put A=U∩V, B=U\V and C=V\U. The constraints act on disjoint blocks A×A (both covers), B×U (row cover) and V×C (column cover), leaving the same free rectangle. Inclusion–exclusion, including H_0=1, gives the overlap factor. Choosing the intersection and then both disjoint differences gives the parameter multiplicities; equal numerical sizes are combined. The singleton count follows in either overlap case. At the complete relation, the first-order zero-line probability is 2n 2^(-n), with Bonferroni error bounded by the sum over pairs, each probability ≤2^(1−2n). Independent entrywise Boolean multiplication exhausts all partners and rectangles for n≤3, and all partners for the three a=b=2 overlap representatives at n=4, recovering 1312,160,128. value.rationale: Centralizer size is the degree count (with the relevant trivial vertices and self counted as commuting partners) in a natural commuting problem. A count across the entire nonzero rank-one stratum is useful even without a higher-rank classification. The formula resolves why overlap changes sizes at the same two support cardinalities, and quantifies nearly universal versus exponentially rare commutation within one rank stratum. It is neither a finite-table extrapolation nor a count only of rectangle-to-rectangle products.
